title: New York musicians and being beaten down by Leonard Davis
summary: The New York musicians' attitude scared him; Joe and Chu bought him gin and told him to stomp on the first trumpeter, and he never looked back.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Going back to when you first came to New York, was there anything like different about working in New York as opposed to where you've been before? Like, were the audiences different? Was there more pressure on the musicians?

No. But the musicians themselves were different. The New York musician, having been here, has a certain attitude, you know. For instance, like, I used to blow out my jaw like Dizzy did, you know. And I played so hard, I found that was the wrong thing for me to do, because my jaws would be all split inside.

But on the... For instance, I'll give you an example. When I first came here, I got in this band, and first of all, I never played in the band with a good string bass and a good drummer with that kind of time, with the sock cymbal, you know. I hadn't played with that. And it was different, you know. Plus, these cats were playing so great, man, and I was scared to death, you know. And every time I'd have a chorus come up, just...the first trumpet player, who was Leonard Davis, he would take my part, you know. Then when I did get something, I was so beaten down then, that I just

couldn't play nothin', you know.
So eventually my brother and Chu got me and took me up to the bar across the street, the Renaissance, and bought me three shillies(?) of gin or corn, whatever it was, and said, "If you don't play, we're gonna kick the shit out of you. Forget this cat. Stomp him." See, we used to... In those days, if you would take my chorus, near the end of your chorus I would stomp on you. That means I'm comin' in! So open the door, right? About the time that we got back on... Because we used to have to play for basketball games at the Rennie. By the time we got back on, man, I was feelin' no pain.

And then my little oats got up, because you know... Because they told me, "He's a first trumpet player. He can't play no Jazz!" So the cat, he took my chorus from me, and I stomped on him! And I ain't looked back since. Heh-heh-heh... He had bugged me, though, by taking my choruses.
